programme: TEAD4 (Hippo-YAP effector), TP53, and RUNX1 form the growth-control axis that decides whether epithelial/mesenchymal cells arrest or proliferate: TP53 is the brake, TEAD4-YAP is the accelerator that TP53 normally keeps in check, and RUNX1 sits alongside them as a lineage/fibrosis-linked cofactor recurrently rewired in the same tumours where TEAD4 and TP53 are disrupted.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, SARS-CoV-2 NSP13 directly suppresses upstream Hippo kinases to release TEAD4-YAP activity, pushing infected/damaged epithelium toward a proliferative repair programme; RUNX1 is separately documented in the multi-organ fibrotic remodeling that follows severe infection; TP53's high Open Targets association reflects the DNA-damage/apoptotic response engaged by viral injury, i.e. the same brake being tested by the same accelerator.
role_in_b: In sarcoma this is the textbook driver axis: TP53 loss or hypomorphism (Li-Fraumeni-associated) removes the brake on mesenchymal proliferation, RUNX1/RUNX2 dysregulation is a direct oncogenic mechanism in specific subtypes (Ewing's sarcoma, myeloid sarcoma), and TEAD4/YAP-Hippo hyperactivation is a recurrent pan-cancer proliferative signal that extends into sarcoma.
shared_axis: Both diseases independently lean on the same TEAD4-TP53-RUNX1 growth-control machinery to decide proliferation versus arrest in damaged or transformed mesenchymal/epithelial tissue: SARS-CoV-2 actively hijacks it for a proliferative/fibrotic repair response after lung injury, while sarcomas arise when the same brake (TP53) fails and the same accelerators (TEAD4-YAP, RUNX1) are constitutively engaged. No paper studies the two diseases together through this axis; the claim is that they converge on the same pathway components, not that one causes or predicts the other.
reasoning: Each carrying factor is independently and specifically documented, not just co-listed: TEAD4 has a direct SARS-CoV-2 mechanistic paper and a direct pan-cancer/sarcoma biomarker paper, and all three factors (TEAD4, TP53, RUNX1) show bilateral above-median Open Targets association in both diseases (unlike the immune-leaning factors STAT4/NFKBIZ/BCL11B, whose OT scores are lopsided toward one disease). That bilateral, factor-level placement is why this clears 'supported' rather than 'unexpected.' It stays at 'moderate' because the cross-disease bridge itself — why a viral-lung-injury programme and a mesenchymal-tumour programme would share this axis — rests on known Hippo–p53–RUNX pathway crosstalk reasoning, not on a paper that studies COVID-19 and sarcoma together through it (36709793 only partially bridges TEAD4 across the two).
support: 40985618 shows SARS-CoV-2 NSP13 suppresses Hippo signaling to activate TEAD in COVID-19; 41098715 places TEAD4 as a pan-cancer prognostic biomarker including sarcoma; 36709793 compares COVID-19 transcriptional signatures against pan-cancer expression data and is the one retrieved paper that touches both diseases through TEAD4; 42605788, 42283722, 42183905 and 42448860 place TP53 mutation/variant biology directly in sarcoma-associated syndromes and tumours; 42499721, 42208169 and 41482356 place RUNX1(/RUNX2) directly in sarcoma pathogenesis (myeloid sarcoma, core-binding-factor translocation, Ewing's sarcoma repression of EWS-FLI1); 40356603 places RUNX factors in multi-organ fibrosis, relevant to but not specific to COVID-19 lung pathology.
how_to_falsify: In SARS-CoV-2-infected airway or endothelial cultures, pharmacologically or genetically block TEAD-YAP activity (e.g. verteporfin or TEAD palmitoylation inhibitors) and test whether this blunts NSP13-driven proliferative/repair transcription and any accompanying RUNX1 induction; separately, in TP53-mutant sarcoma lines, test TEAD4 dependency (CRISPR knockout or ChIP for TEAD4/RUNX1 co-occupancy at shared proliferative targets). If TEAD4 inhibition does not affect the COVID-relevant proliferative programme, or TP53 status does not modulate TEAD4/RUNX1 dependency in sarcoma lines, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (COVID-19) against soft tissue (sarcoma) — a real anatomical stretch, which is why the account is framed as a shared systemic growth-control pathway rather than a tissue-identity link. 40 patient-group comparisons come from only 6 independent cohort pairs, so some of the concordance is not fully independent. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed STAT1, IRF4, IRF5, IRF8, NFATC1 and CIITA — the classic interferon/immune master regulators for blood and immune tissue — which is why an interferon/immune-cell story was not built here; that omission is the reason those factors are absent, not an oversight. Single-view exclusions (KDM5D, BRCA1, SOX5, etc.) confirm the retained factors are not artifacts of one aberrant patient subgroup. Four of the twelve concordant factors (ZNF256, MEIS3, MLXIP, TSHZ1) carry no literature or Open Targets support for either disease and were left out of the programme as uninformative, along with BCL11B, STAT4, NFKBIZ, ATF5 and DLX5, whose disease-association evidence was too one-sided or too generic (pan-cancer, not sarcoma-specific) to carry this particular account.
